nodes.name: lem:time-size: Time vs Space
nodes.statement:
Let $T(n)\ge n$ be a time function.
The following three are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item All CorePolyC programs have an instruction count of $O(T(n))$.
    \item All CorePolyC programs only produce outputs of size $O(T(n))$.
    \item All CorePolyC programs only generate values of size $O(T(n))$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: prop:prog-size: Programs
nodes.statement: Given a program $\mathsf{p}$, it holds that $\vert\llbracket\mathsf{p}\rrbracket_{}(\widetilde{v})\vert=O(\mathtt{poly}(n))$.

nodes.name: lem:stmt-invariant: Statements
lem:expr-size: Expressions
lem:op-size: Operators
nodes.statement: For any $\mathtt{op}\in\mathsf{O}$, $\vert\llbracket\mathtt{op}\rrbracket_{}(\widetilde{v})\vert\le\max_{i=1}^{m} \vert v_i\vert+k$, where $k$ is a constant.

nodes.name: lem:simulate: Simulation
nodes.statement: Every polynomial-time Turing machine can be simulated by a CorePolyC program, and such a program can be constructed in polynomial time.

nodes.name: lemma:poly-con: Clock
nodes.statement: For each $d\geq 1$, there exists an $O(d\log d)$-size program $\mathsf{p}$ such that $\vert\llbracket\mathsf{p}\rrbracket_{}{(v)}\vert= d\vert v\vert^d$.
